metadata.title: Free IQ Test: 30 Matrix Reasoning Questions & Free Results
metadata.description: FermatMind IQ: 30 original visual matrix questions, ~20 min. Free test and results. Review reasoning, scores and limits; no substitute for professional IQ assessment.

faq_items.question: What does the FermatMind IQ test measure? Is it a complete intelligence assessment?
faq_items.answer: It observes performance on the current original 30-question visual matrix reasoning form, involving visual pattern recognition and abstract relationships. It does not cover every cognitive domain or equal a comprehensive professional intelligence assessment.

faq_items.question: How many questions are there, and how long does it take? Is it an official Raven or Mensa test?
faq_items.answer: The current public version has 30 original questions and an estimated duration of about 20 minutes. Estimated time is neither an intelligence threshold nor a confirmed hard time limit. This is not an official Raven or Mensa admission test or proof of authorisation by those organisations.

faq_items.question: How are raw scores and accuracy calculated?
faq_items.answer: Each correct answer earns 1 point and an incorrect answer earns 0, giving a raw score of 0–30. Eighteen correct answers mean 18/30 and 60% accuracy; 60% describes the proportion correct, not IQ 60 or the 60th percentile.

faq_items.question: Do item-group scores represent independent abilities?
faq_items.answer: Item-group scores summarise performance on the items in that group. Grouping and naming do not establish validated ability subscales and cannot generate stable intelligence types.

faq_items.question: Does Beta 121 mean IQ 121?
faq_items.answer: No. Beta uses a simulated random-response baseline rather than representative population norms. Eight correct answers give 121 under the current public formula, but this is not population IQ or a population ranking; the existence of the formula also does not guarantee that the current report interface displays it.

faq_items.question: Why do different results produce the same Beta?
faq_items.answer: The indicator is capped at 145, and every current integer correct count from 12–30 maps to 145. It therefore cannot distinguish the raw results in that range. Zero correct answers produce 62; 55 is only the configured lower bound.

faq_items.question: Can IQ scores from different websites be compared directly?
faq_items.answer: Not from the numbers alone. Coverage, item difficulty, age references, language, administration conditions and score conversions can differ. Interchangeable scores across versions require evidence; do not convert similar-looking numbers yourself.

faq_items.question: What evidence should I check when asking whether an online IQ test is accurate?
faq_items.answer: Check the particular tool’s coverage, age and language suitability, scoring, sample sources, reliability and validity for its intended use. Online delivery alone neither establishes measurement validity nor invalidates every online tool.

faq_items.question: Can I use AI, search or another person’s help?
faq_items.answer: Answer on your own if you want to observe independent performance. An assisted score reflects different conditions; record that qualification and do not compare it directly with independent completion.

faq_items.question: Does a higher score after practice mean intelligence has increased?
faq_items.answer: Not necessarily. Familiarity with item types, changed strategies, remembered answers or better response conditions can all affect scores. You can observe strategy use on entirely new materials, but one score increase does not establish growth in general intelligence.

faq_items.question: Is the test free? How should low scores, children’s results or certificates be understood?
faq_items.answer: This site’s current original 30-question test and results are free. A result is not a certification or diagnostic certificate. A low score does not encompass every ability or future potential; without clear age validation and norms, do not use it for childhood assessment, educational placement or cross-age rankings.

entry_fields.title: IQ (Intelligence Quotient) Test
entry_fields.description: Assess matrix reasoning, pattern recognition and abstract problem-solving ability.
audience: People who want a focused initial screening before deciding whether to explore further.
People comparing their personal patterns across work, learning, relationships and management of their current state.
People who want to continue reviewing and reading after the results page.
entry_fields.when_to_use: Use this assessment when you want to complete 30 questions in about 20 minutes and gain a clearer sense of your next step.
how_it_works: Complete 30 questions in one focused session.
View the generated results summary immediately after submitting your answers.
Use the core result to choose a more detailed report, guide or related content.
When your circumstances change, retake the test and compare it with your earlier baseline.

highlight.excerpt: Work through matrix-reasoning and pattern-analysis questions to observe your current problem-solving approach. The result is not a fixed judgment of intelligence or potential.
highlight.seo_copy: This IQ test focuses on matrix reasoning and pattern analysis for self-assessment reference; it does not determine fixed intelligence, potential, admission or hiring outcomes.
